title: Multi-stage builds
summary: Build with the SDK, ship only the runtime: multi-stage Dockerfiles for .NET and Next.js.

steps.title: Build tools do not belong in production
body: Compiling needs the SDK, compilers, package caches and source code. Running needs only the output and a runtime. A **multi-stage** Dockerfile has several `FROM` lines; each starts a fresh stage, and only the **last** stage becomes the image. `COPY --from=<stage>` pulls files out of an earlier one.
# ---- stage 1: build with the full SDK (~800 MB) ----
# ---- stage 2: run with only the ASP.NET runtime (~220 MB) ----

The final image contains the aspnet base layers, `WORKDIR` and the published files, nothing from the build stage. Smaller to push and pull, and far less software for an attacker (or a CVE scanner) to find.

steps.prompt: In the Dockerfile above, which of these ends up in the final image?
options: The published `Api.dll` and the ASP.NET Core runtime
The .NET SDK and the NuGet package cache
steps.explain: Only the last stage ships. The build stage is a scratch area whose results you pick from with `COPY --from`.
`aspnet` has the ASP.NET Core runtime; `runtime` has only the base .NET runtime (fine for console apps); `runtime-deps` has neither (for self-contained apps).

steps.title: The same idea for Node and Next.js
body: A Next.js app needs dev dependencies (TypeScript, the compiler) to build, but with `output: "standalone"` in `next.config.js`, the build emits a minimal server with only the modules it needs:
Three stages: install once (cached until the lock file changes), build, then a runner that never sees the full `node_modules`.

steps.prompt: Match each stage of the Next.js Dockerfile to its job.
pairs: installs node_modules from the lock file, cached separately
compiles the app with dev dependencies available
the shipped image: standalone server, static files, non-root user
picks build outputs into the runner

steps.prompt: After a multi-stage build of the Next.js app, where does each thing live?
How do you build only up to the `build` stage, for example to run the tests inside it in CI?
steps.explain: `--target` stops at the named stage, which is a neat way to run `dotnet test` in the same environment the release is built in.

steps.title: Map the stages
prompt: Write `List<string> Stages(List<string> lines)` that describes a multi-stage Dockerfile:
- each `FROM image [AS name]` adds `stage NAME from IMAGE`; an unnamed stage is named by its 0-based index (`0`, `1`, ...);
- each `COPY` with a `--from=X` token adds `  CURRENT copies from X` (two leading spaces; CURRENT is the stage it appears in);
- finally add `final image: NAME` for the last stage.
Keywords may be in any case (`as`, `from`). Ignore every other instruction.
solution: string name = t.Length >= 4 && t[2].ToUpper() == "AS" ? t[3] : names.Count.ToString();
template: Dojo.Eq(".NET two-stage", new List<string> { "stage build from mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0", "stage final from mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0", "  final copies from build", "final image: final" }, Stages(new List<string> { "FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build", "WORKDIR /src", "COPY . .", "RUN dotnet publish -o /app/publish", "FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 AS final", "COPY --from=build /app/publish ." }));

Dojo.Eq("Next.js three-stage", new List<string> { "stage deps from node:22-alpine", "stage build from node:22-alpine", "  build copies from deps", "stage runner from node:22-alpine", "  runner copies from build", "  runner copies from build", "final image: runner" }, Stages(new List<string> { "FROM node:22-alpine AS deps", "RUN npm ci", "FROM node:22-alpine AS build", "COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules", "COPY . .", "from node:22-alpine as runner", "COPY --from=build /app/.next/standalone ./", "COPY --from=build /app/public ./public" }));

Dojo.Eq("unnamed stages use indexes", new List<string> { "stage 0 from golang:1.23", "stage 1 from scratch", "  1 copies from 0", "final image: 1" }, Stages(new List<string> { "FROM golang:1.23", "RUN go build -o /app", "FROM scratch", "COPY --from=0 /app /app" }));
hints: Keep a list of stage names; the current stage is the last one in it.
